_boardComment: All nineteen test points are placed by hand, as a matter of course. On this
drawing the wire loop is printed as a short bar beside its label -- under it
for TP1, TP2, TP3, TP5, TP19, above it for TP6, TP8, TP16, to the right for
TP4 and TP9, to the left for TP7 and TP17 -- so every box below spans label
and pad together rather than the lettering alone.
The rest are parts §5-4 or a 3900-series fault code names, whose reader
marker was on a neighbour's label or was never found at all. C8 is the one
worth singling out: the reader had it on C83, which arrived in the agreed
tier looking trustworthy.
A later pass placed the 77 remaining electrical parts that had no board
position at all. Where the designator is printed inside a printed outline --
the boxed capacitors, the four chokes, the TO-92 pair and every can -- the
marker is that outline: flood-filled from the designator for the boxes,
fitted to the arcs by a Hough search for the round bodies, measured off a
pixel grid for the four capsule-shaped chokes. Where the designator is
printed beside its part, as most resistors and diodes are, the marker is a
tight box on the lettering.
Fourteen of the 77 are the truncation misreads listed under drop below, now
measured: C1, C6, C7, C10, C56, Q7, R3, R7, R8, R12, R14, R15, R16 and R96.
The drop entries stay, so removing a hand position here cannot quietly bring
the wrong reader marker back. The other 63 the reader never found at all.

_dropComment: Markers that pointed at another part's label. A marker on the wrong part is
worse than no marker at all -- it sends a probe to the wrong pad and the
coverage badge still counts the part as placed -- so these are dropped and
the parts are reported unplaced until someone measures them.
Most are truncation misreads of a longer designator on the same drawing:
C6 and C10 are C61 and C75, C7 is C14, R7 is R97, R12 is R124, R14 is R74,
R16 is R76, R96 is R98, C56 is C58, R8 is R83, R3 is VR3, C1 is C17, Q7 is
L21, R15 is R16, U5 and J1 both landed on the 'USA' of MADE IN USA. R45 is
the interesting one: the silkscreen there really does read CR45, a diode
position that appears in neither parts list -- see the caveat.
CP1, H1, H7, M5 and W2 are dropped as well because they have no silkscreen
designator at all and belong in notOnDrawing below.
_schematicComment: Positions measured by hand on the sheets, in pixels of each sheet's own
full-resolution crop. Two kinds of entry: test points the reader found only
in the sheet 1 legend table (so its marker answered a question nobody asked)
and now sit on the flag symbol on their own net, and contested markers that
turned out to be right, promoted so their badge stops warning about a
disagreement that has been settled.
Every test point placement was cross-checked against the signal name printed
beside the symbol and against the legend's own zone reference -- TP1 = RMS
SENSOR DC (PG1B4) really is in sheet 1 zone B4, TP7 = SENSOR INPUT (PG1D5) in
zone D5.
A third pass filled the 71 parts that had a board position and no sheet
position at all. Every one of them turned out to be printed in the circuit
body of a sheet -- none of the 71 is board-only hardware -- so all 71 are
placed here: 19 on sheet 1, 38 on sheet 2, 14 on sheet 3, with K9 and K11
on two sheets each (contacts on sheet 1, coil on sheet 3).
The six 6T chokes divide by supply: L1 and L2 are the +17S/-17S pair in
sheet 1's P111 block, L3 to L6 the +5RLH/RLHCOM/+5LH/-5LH set in sheet 3's,
and L18 is in sheet 2's X10 amplifier. W1 is printed inside the FERRITE
BEAD box on sheet 1 and E1 is the bus-wire link above Q11 on sheet 2, so
even the wire and cable entries have a place on a sheet.
Each position was read off a labelled pixel grid over the full-resolution
crop and then checked by rendering the marker back onto the sheet.
A fourth pass followed the board pass that placed the last 77 parts: 35 of
those 77 had no sheet position either. They divide 8 / 24 / 3 across sheets
1, 2 and 3, and again every one is drawn in a circuit body. Two are worth
naming. Q18's designator is printed twice on sheet 3 -- once in the
bottom-view package legend at the foot of the sheet and once beside the
VN0104 driving K1's coil; the position here is the second. And C26 is the
hand-lettered 4.7 uF 25 V across K7's coil, the one ECO addition sheet 3
actually carries, which is why it is drawn in a different hand.

_dropSchematicComment: A sheet is mostly text that is not a designator, and the reader cannot tell
the difference. Every marker on every sheet was rendered and looked at; these
are the ones that had landed on a component value, a net name, a pin number,
a caption or a legend row.
On sheet 1 that was 44 of 130. Twelve of them were the sheet's own test point
legend table, which is crisper text than the flag symbols on the nets and so
the reader prefers it -- TP7 to TP14 and TP17 all landed there, and eight of
those points are not on sheet 1 at all. Four more were the ATTENUATORS and
OVERLOAD CONTROL CIRCUIT captions and the NOTES block.
Note what is NOT dropped: the K4-K8 blocks in the attenuator section look
like the bottom-view legends the pitfalls warn about, dashed outline and a
TO-5 package note, but they are the relay contacts drawn in circuit under the
ATTENUATORS caption. They are correct.
Sheet 2 lost 30 of 99. It is the densest sheet -- three amplifier stages,
sixteen transistors and a hundred component values -- and almost every wrong
marker had landed on a value or a device type: K5 on 'MRF544', VR1 on
'MRF545', C5 on a relay pin number, Z2 on the word CONNECTION.
Sheet 3 lost 55 of 93, the worst of the three, and it fails in the two ways
the pitfalls name. Its bottom-view pinout legends are captioned with the
designators they apply to -- 'K4-K8', 'K2, K3, K9, K10, K12', 'Q4, Q5, Q6',
'Q7-Q16' -- and the reader placed a marker on each caption: K11, L1, M5, Q1,
Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q17, J1, J2, J3, R8 and C9 are all that one block. Its
relay state table's column headers are nothing but designators, which took
M2, R15 and Q10. And its notes paragraph names K9 and Q18 in prose, which
took those two. Find those three blocks before reviewing anything else on a
sheet like this.
What is kept on sheet 3 is the relay coils themselves (K1-K8, K10, K12 in
their 2FCL/4FCL and TO-5 drive blocks), the supply decoupling, the 82C55 and
the three drivers, and the six 10 ohm coil resistors R123-R128 -- which are
the parts that put those six designators on this board in the first place.
C57 is the one marker on these sheets that was wrong and had nowhere else to
be: the reader read the word RST inside K1's coil block on sheet 3 as C57,
and that was C57's only schematic position. It is dropped here and placed by
hand on sheet 2, at Q11's emitter where it is actually drawn.
_notOnDrawingComment: Parts in the list of replaceable parts that carry no silkscreen designator
on the assembly drawing: the four sheet-metal shields, the ejectors, the
rivets, the screws, the transistor mounting insulators and heat spreaders,
the C-MOS instruction label, and the accessories the wideband option ships
with (CP1-CP3, the N-type termination MP1 and the output cable W2). They
stay in the parts list and remain searchable, but counting them as unplaced
would make the coverage badge lie.
E3 is here for a different reason: it is a real, removable link that §5-4
steps 6 and 8 tell you to pull, but the board silkscreens only the header it
plugs onto. Look for J3, which is placed.
C30, C31, C32 and R45 were added when the board pass ran out of parts to
place. C30 and C31 exist only in the 1996 revision of the 0.1 uF polyester
row, C32 only in its first tantalum row; Rev 9 has none of the three, no
sheet draws one, and neither an OCR sweep nor a look at the drawing finds a
silkscreen -- the two caveats in a5.reference.json carry the working. R45 is
real and is drawn on sheet 3, but the only candidate lettering on the
drawing reads CR45, so R45 carries no designator of its own here.
_layersComment: Registration of the photograph against the locator drawing, from which
build_coords.py solves the board -> photo homography. 'src' is board space
(the drawing), 'dst' is photo space; both are normalised, not pixels.
This board was carried for a while as the one assembly with no registered
photograph, on the stated grounds that the attenuator shields were fitted
and hid everything left of x=0.28. That was wrong, and it is the reason
this took a year to happen. Nothing on this board is shielded or covered:
M2-M5 are all off. The pale rectangle at the left that reads as a shield
lid is the PTFE RF laminate the attenuator is built on -- part of the board
itself, with its own plated via ring, its own pads and its own yellow
silkscreen, all of it legible: Z1, Z2, K4-K9, C25-C37, C30-C33, R43, R44.
The blue PCB edge runs round all four sides of it. The K4-K8 relay cans,
the two SIP attenuator networks and K9's Aromat relay are sitting on it in
plain view. It runs x 0.03 to 0.26 and y 0.31 to 0.69 of the photograph;
K7, K4, K5 and C28 below are landmarks on it, and the left-hand end is
anchored no worse than the middle -- the opposite of the A11 case the note
was reasoning from. A photograph is worth opening before writing down what
it shows.
Every 'src' below is a board position already reviewed marker by marker and
sitting in the 'board' block or the reader's own placement, so each pair is
a correspondence someone can check -- open the drawing at K5 and the
photograph at K5 and see the same relay -- rather than a sample of a matrix.
The matching 'dst' was found by cross-correlation: the locator drawing *is*
the silkscreen artwork and the photograph shows the same artwork in yellow
ink, so a yellow-ink mask of the photo (R-B against a local background,
which keeps the silkscreen on both the blue and the white areas and drops
the substrate itself) was thinned to strokes, warped into board space and
matched patch by patch against the drawing's own ink, and the fit re-solved
and re-matched until it stopped moving. Which peaks to believe was decided
by RANSAC over all 213 placements rather than by whether the running fit
liked them. None of the landmarks is on a designator's *text*: the drawing
prints much of that inside the part outline where the board prints it
outside, so a 160 px patch is matched on the outlines around the point and
the offset that wins is applied to the reviewed coordinate.
Nothing here is on an ejector lever, a mounting hole or a standoff. Both
ejectors are photographed out of the position the drawing draws them in --
the left one folded down over the board edge, the right one standing up --
so besides the parallax references/pitfalls.md warns about, they are not
even in the right place.
How good it is, measured rather than asserted. The same cross-correlation
was run at all 213 reviewed board positions; 112 of them locked onto one
place unambiguously and are the population the fit was judged against. The
101 that did not are either buried under a component -- this board is dense
with toroids and axial parts lying across their own silkscreen -- or sit in
a run of identical resistors where the peak jumps to the neighbour. Against
those 112 the shipped homography lands a median 2.1 px, p90 3.5 px and
worst 6.6 px out, in pixels of the 3400 px photo the browser loads --
better than A20's 4.8/8.6/13.4 and A19's 3.7/11.2/15.0. The 32 landmarks
kept below are one per cell of a 12x4 grid over the board, chosen by peak
sharpness, and the homography they give agrees with the one fitted to all
112 to within 4.0 px everywhere on the board, i.e. the fit is anchored
across the whole board rather than in one region and extrapolated.
The board outline was fitted first, independently, to start the search: the
blue PCB edge segments cleanly against the light background all the way
round, and iterative closest point on that contour -- with the ejectors and
the P111 connector shell excluded, since neither is in the board's plane --
lands the drawing's outline a median 2.0 px from the photographed edge. It
is a good start and it is not the answer: that fit and the silkscreen fit
differ by a median 8 px and up to 25 px at the corners, and under the
silkscreen fit the drawing's outline sits a median 8.6 px outside the
photographed edge. The edge is not in the silkscreen's plane -- the camera
sees the top face of a 1.6 mm board from above and the segmentation takes
the shadow with it -- so an edge-only registration is off by that much
everywhere the markers actually are. Fit the edge to start; land the
answer on the artwork.
Checked the way that actually catches a bad fit: all 213 reviewed markers
were drawn onto the photograph through this homography and looked at, tile
by tile, from R124-R128 and TP2 at the top left through the K4-K9
attenuator, W1, the MRF544/MRF545 output stage and the 82C55 to
R54-R70/TP11/C47-C49 at the right-hand end. Every one lands on its own
part. Two are worth knowing about rather than fixing: W1's marker is the
drawing's straight coax run and the photographed cable is dressed at an
angle across it, and R54/R61 sit under the Q7/Q8 toroids, so their markers
land on the toroid that covers them.
